page.layout: One printed page. A single column of index lines from top to bottom, each ending in a folio reference set at the right. Below the list, a central fleuron ornament. No margin notes, running head, page number or catchword.

main_text.l: De Tentoriis, Fosså, Vallo, Portis. Dial.v. fol.53.
De operibus, qui Immunes in iis, qui Munifices. Socordia posterioris ævi. Dial.vi. fol.67.
De Ministeriis, quæ Tribunis & Equitibus & alibi præstantur, item de Excubiis & Stationibus. Dial.viii. fol.78.
De Vigiliis. Tessera in iis, Tesserulæ, & divisio, & Circuitio, omnia distinctè. Dial.ix. fol.90.
De imperiis castrorum, & administratione in his talibus. Tribuni per vices faciunt. & Salutationes ducum. Dial.x. fol.119.
Ad Exercitia transitum. Ea divisa, & primò dictum de Oneris exercitiis. Tulisse cibos, vallos, sarcinas, præter arma. Dial.xi. fol.124.
De Agmine toto. tum de metatione castrorum, & metatoribus. Dial.xii. fol.134.
De Exercitio Operis. Exempla aliquot eiusmodi illustria, Dialog.xiii. fol.148.
Armorum exercitia, quàm crebra, & quàm passim? Tum ordine quædam data. Dial.xiiii. fol.155.
Ad Leges itum, ac primò de eâ quæ Furta tangit, tum quæ Prædam. Dial.xv. fol.167.
De stipendio militum, eius origine & auctu. De Frumenti modo, & hordei. de iis quæ ad victum. Dial.xvi. fol.172.
Præmia militaria, hastæ, Armillæ, Torques, Phaleræ, Spolia. Dial. xvii. fol.193.
De pœnis, quis inflixerit, & quas: tum etiam de variis ignominiis. Dialog.xviii. fol.210.
De Missione quadruplici, Honestâ, Caussariâ, Gratiosâ, Ignominiosâ: & de Commodis missorum. Dial.xix. fol.232.
Conclusio sermonum quinque, & militiæ veteris cum nostrâ breuis comparatio. Dial. xx. fol.237.

page.notes: Central fleuron ornament (woodcut, grotesque mask with scrollwork and pendant) below the list, not transcribed. Faint show-through text in the lower half of the page and mirrored text at the right edge is ignored. The "Dial.xix." line has the folio "fol.232." printed slightly lower; the reading is clear. Spelling normalised to u/v and i/j rules where the printer used j or i as a vowel (e.g. "iis", "Ministeriis"); the printed forms were "ijs", "Ministerijs", etc. Ligatures and printed spacing otherwise follow the scan.
